en.name: Anuarite Nengapeta
en.summary: Congolese religious sister killed resisting a rebel commander's demands during the civil conflict that followed Congolese independence.
en.body: Marie-Clementine Anuarite Nengapeta was a young member of the Congolese religious congregation of the Holy Family, serving at a convent school in what was then eastern Zaire during the chaotic civil conflict that engulfed the newly independent country in the 1960s. When rebel forces overran the region, she and her fellow sisters were taken captive, and a rebel commander singled her out, demanding she become his mistress; when she refused despite repeated threats, he stabbed her to death in 1964, reportedly in a rage after her continued resistance. Her death drew wide attention as an example of steadfast resistance to sexual violence amid the wider brutality of the conflict, and devotion to her spread quickly within the Congolese Catholic community. She was beatified by Pope John Paul II in Kinshasa in 1985, the first beatification held on African soil, and remains one of the most venerated modern martyrs of the African Church, with her cause for canonization ongoing.
